title: Azure Managed Redis Onboarding Request
description: Schema for one onboarding request file consumed by the Terraform root under config/onboarding-files-redis/*.json. This is the exact shape the UI/wrapper API must produce — every field name, nesting level, and allowed value here is read verbatim by locals.tf. Fields not listed here are ignored by Terraform even if present. This file is a reference for the UI team, not itself read by Terraform.

type.description: Structural marker. Always the literal string "instance". Not used by Terraform (filtered by filename, not this field), but keep it for consistency with default.json's own "type" marker.

request_type.description: "create" covers BOTH creating a new instance and updating an existing one — there is no separate "update" value. To change an existing instance, resubmit the same file with the same instance.name and the changed field(s). "delete" removes the instance from the next Terraform apply; the instance object can be left in place as a historical record.

environment.description: Which environment this request applies to. Must match one of default.json's environments.<env> keys exactly. Determines subscription_id, resource group, default location, and VNet/subnet — and also becomes this instance's `environment` Azure tag automatically (the UI does not need a separate field for that tag).

requested_by.description: Free-text requester identity (e.g. team name, username). Not validated or used by Terraform beyond being stored in the request file; purely a paper trail.

name.description: Base name for the instance. Terraform appends "-<environment>" automatically to build the real Azure resource name (e.g. "my-cache" + dev -> "my-cache-dev") — do NOT include the environment in this field. MUST be unique across every request file targeting the same environment; two files with the same name silently collide and only one instance gets created (this template's request_names_unique_per_environment check catches this at plan time). Keep it short.

location.description: Azure region for the PRIMARY instance, e.g. "eastus2". Optional — omit to use the environment's default location (default.json.environments.<env>.location). Any Azure region is accepted as-is (this template maintains no allow-list). Only matters for DR: cross-region replication is currently only supported between the specific pairs listed in default.json.dr_region_pairs (see deployment_topology below) — requesting DR-ActivePassive/DR-ActiveActive from a primary location outside a supported pair fails plan-time validation.

deployment_topology.description: The single topology knob — there is no separate replica_count or cross_region_replica field the way some other onboarding flows split this into. STANDALONE: no HA, no DR. HA: HA/zone redundancy enabled, single region. DR-ActivePassive: adds a standalone standby DR instance in the paired region (kept in sync out-of-band — see the redis module's README). DR-ActiveActive: adds a DR instance live-linked via geo-replication; persistence is automatically disabled in this mode regardless of the persistence block below.

node_type.description: Azure Managed Redis SKU. Please select one of the Balanced_Bxx options unless advised by engineering or Redis support. Changing this on an existing instance forces replacement (Azure API behavior).
node_type.x-notes: No fixed default here — the UI should require an explicit choice, or default.json.node_type ("Balanced_B0") is used if omitted.

authorization_mode.description: Client authentication mode. AccessKey is fully self-service — works end to end through this onboarding flow. MicrosoftEntraID disables access-key auth, but requires the platform team to grant specific principals data-plane access OUT OF BAND (Azure Portal/CLI) after this request applies — no Terraform automation exists for that grant yet. Do not let a UI submit MicrosoftEntraID without surfacing that manual follow-up step to the requester.

persistence.description: All sub-fields are optional and merged individually against default.json's persistence block — you can set just `mode` and still inherit the matching rdb/aof frequency default. Automatically forced to DISABLED (regardless of what's requested here) whenever deployment_topology = DR-ActiveActive.

deletion_protection_enabled.description: When true, an Azure resource lock (CanNotDelete) is created on the instance — deletion is blocked at the Azure Portal/CLI/API level, not just a Terraform-side guard. Must be explicitly set back to false in a prior apply before a delete request can succeed. Also blocks any change that forces resource replacement (e.g. node_type) until temporarily disabled.

geo_replication_group_name.description: Optional name override for the geo-replication group. Only relevant when deployment_topology = DR-ActiveActive; ignored otherwise. Leave unset to let Azure generate one.
geo_replication_group_name.x-notes: Present in the schema for completeness; most requests should omit this.

application_id.description: Instance-level field (NOT nested under `tags`). Always becomes the `application_id` Azure tag. Optional — falls back to default.json's `default_application_id` if omitted.

lob.description: Instance-level field (NOT nested under `tags`). Always becomes the `lob` (line of business / cost center) Azure tag if provided. No default — omitted entirely from tags if not set.

tags.description: OPTIONAL free-form extra tags, entirely at the requester's discretion — anything set here is appended to the instance's Azure tags alongside application_id/lob. Most requests can omit this entirely. Do NOT put `topology`, `environment`, or `managed_by` in here — those three keys are always overwritten by Terraform-derived values regardless of what's sent, so a UI should either omit them as options or grey them out.

client_protocol.description: NOT a request field. Every instance is created with client_protocol = Encrypted — enforced by the Terraform module itself (validation rejects any other value); there is no override. Do not expose this as a UI field.

public_network_access.description: NOT a request field. Every instance is created with public_network_access = Disabled — enforced by the Terraform module itself; there is no override. Do not expose this as a UI field.

x-fields-never-in-request.description: These are computed entirely by Terraform and must never be exposed as UI inputs, even read-only ones that echo a value back — showing them invites someone to eventually try to set them.
fields: resource_group_name / subnet_name / vnet_name / vnet_resource_group_name / dr_subnet_name / dr_vnet_name / dr_vnet_resource_group_name (always environment infra from default.json, never instance-settable)
dr_location (derived from location via dr_region_pairs, only when deployment_topology is one of the DR-* values)
tags.topology / tags.environment / tags.managed_by (always overwritten by Terraform even if present in tags)
client_protocol / public_network_access (hard-fixed by the Terraform module to Encrypted / Disabled)
